item.description:
# LocalXiv 0.0.18
Read arXiv papers comfortably on your Mac, then take them to Kindle. This preview redesigns the app as a native Mac window, keeps your place in every paper, shows citations and figures where you read, and lets you check every Blog claim against the passage it cites.
## Changes
- **Native Mac window.** AppKit now draws the window around the reader. The sidebar shows Home, the Library views with counts, and the papers you opened last; in a paper it shows the outline of the current view and marks the section you read. The toolbar holds back and forward, the Overview, Blog, and Paper switch, **Aa**, **More**, and **Search**. The menu bar has File, Edit, View, Paper, Go, and Window menus with shortcuts, and **⌘,** opens a Settings window with panes. The page lies under the toolbar and sidebar glass, and the Reading theme sets the window's appearance. - **Reading.** Text is 18 px with a line height of 1.55 in a column of about 68 characters. **Aa** sets the theme (Light, Sepia, Dark, or Match System), the font (New York, Charter, Iowan Old Style, Palatino, or SF Pro), the size, the margins (Narrow, Normal, or Wide), and the line spacing. The settings keep these choices, so they stay after the app restarts. - **Reference previews.** In the Paper, hover a citation, a figure, table, or equation link, a footnote, or a section link to see its target where you read. Click it to go there, and press **⌘[** to return to the same paragraph. Click a figure to enlarge it, which did not work in the Mac app before. - **Reading state and position.** Each paper is New, Reading, or Read. A paper reopens at its view, chapter, and passage, and the Blog at its section. Home and the Library show Continue reading, and the Library sorts by date added, date read, title, or publication date. - **Blog and Overview.** Each Blog claim has a small citation number. Hover it to see the cited passage, and click it to open the paper there. On a wide window the paper opens beside the explanation. Every Overview and Blog names the model and the date. A Blog section with an em dash goes back for a correction. - **Find and search.** **⌘F** finds text in the open view. Search starts as a magnifier in the toolbar and finds papers in your library and on arXiv as you type. - **Settings and setup.** The Settings window saves each change as you make it. Connection Setup no longer skips itself when you press Return. - **Anthropic.** Anthropic is a provider preset, through the Messages API. - **Removed.** The chat feature, the "Model accepts images" setting, and the image evidence path are gone. The app no longer moves a library from the old PapersToKindle folder. If your library is still there, open 0.0.17 once first. - **Development install.** `install-app.sh` and `launch.command` use Python 3.14 when it is installed, because the pinned `pydantic_core` does not load on Python 3.15.
## Verification and limitations
The release workflow checks the source, builds the portable app, runs native renderer tests, and verifies the packaged runtime after moving the app. Attached assets include the verification report, runtime inventory, exact app source, dependency source inputs, and SHA-256 checksums.
Local verification on the release branch ran 95 component tests and 1 front-end test. 94 component tests and the front-end test passed, and Ruff found no issues. One live test, which calls Semantic Scholar and arXiv, was skipped.
The redesign was checked on copies of a real library: in the browser, in WebKit screenshots of every screen in Light, Sepia, and Dark, and in a native harness that drives the Mac window and records its toolbar, menus, and sidebar. Independent reviews checked each part against its spec. A design audit verified 88 issues; this release fixes every medium issue and most low ones, and the rest are kept with a reason. The production and Sparkle builds compile with no warnings.
Open items:
- Offscreen snapshots cannot draw Liquid Glass. The automated checks cover where the page sits under the glass, not the blur itself. - Sentence copy mixes "Paper" and "paper". - An architecture review lists 12 small removals of unused code for a later release. - Unchanged from 0.0.17: 51 papers in the frozen corpus still fail on the Pandoc route and fall back to arXiv HTML or to the retained PDF.
Offline tests use scripted provider responses. They verify recovery and export behavior, not live-provider reliability, scientific accuracy, generation speed, or cost.
AI explanations remain experimental. Generation may take several minutes or fail, and generated claims need checking against the paper. AI requests send selected paper content to your configured provider and may incur charges. Paper search sends the typed text to Semantic Scholar and arXiv. Importing, reading, and exporting papers do not require AI credentials.
## Installation
Requires Apple Silicon and macOS 26 or newer. Download the DMG and drag LocalXiv into Applications. Finish active jobs before updating. Your library and settings remain on your Mac. Updater-enabled builds can use **LocalXiv → Check for Updates…** once the signed feed is published.
This preview is ad hoc signed, without Apple Developer ID signing or notarization. macOS may block the first launch. The Sparkle update feed is signed separately with the project's local update key. Separate-Mac installation and actual Kindle delivery are not covered by the automated checks.
